title: What do the numbers in the count of five end in?
description: Counting in fives from five builds a strip of numbers, and the video reads the last digit of each one. The pattern finds the largest number below three hundred and ninety nine and settles eight thousand five hundred and sixty, and Keeko's doubt, that only a five at the end will do, is broken.
teaching_notes: One idea: the multiples of five end in zero and five, taking turns. Watch for students who think only a five at the end can show a multiple of five.

source: Look at the multiples of 5. What is the last digit? What is the largest number less than 399 divisible by 5, and is 8560 divisible by 5?
video_script.why: The child sees the pattern in the last digit of the multiples of five and uses it on a number just below three hundred and ninety nine and on eight thousand five hundred and sixty.
video_script.substitution: List the multiples of five, read the last digits, and test any number by its last digit.
video_script.anchor: a strip of number cards counting in fives from 5, with the last digit of each card lit
video_script.wrong_answer: only numbers ending in five are divisible by five
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says only numbers that end in five are divisible by five. Ten, twenty and thirty are in the count of five and end in zero, so the bubble is struck through.
video_script.payoff_line: The last digit is zero or five

final_answer.spoken: the last digit is zero or five, the largest number is three hundred and ninety five, and yes, eight thousand five hundred and sixty is divisible by five

hold_back: Answer: the last digit is 0 or 5; 395; yes
never_show: only numbers ending in 5 are divisible by 5
maths_rules: the last digits go 5, 0, 5, 0, 5, 0, so the last digit is 0 or 5
399 ends in 9, 398 in 8, 397 in 7, 396 in 6, 395 in 5; the largest number below 399 that ends in 0 or 5 is 395
8560 ends in 0, so 5 divides it; 8560 = 5 x 1712
video_script.design: One idea: the last digit of a multiple of five is zero or five. Assumes skip counting. Wrong idea: only a final five counts. The strip stays on the board to the end.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about counting in fives.
<bookmark mark='count'/>The count goes five, ten, fifteen, twenty, twenty five.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What do the last digits show?
What is the largest number below three hundred and ninety nine in the count?

beats.on_screen: the strip holds still and the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: jumps of 5 from zero land on the cards one by one; the label multiple of 5

marks.jump: jumps of five from zero land on the cards one by one
marks.name: the label multiple of 5 is written over the cards

narration: <bookmark mark='jump'/>Start at zero and jump in fives.
<bookmark mark='name'/>Every number you land on is called a multiple of five.

beats.on_screen: Given: the count in fives; the limit 399; the number 8560

marks.given: the count, the limit and the number are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the count in fives.
The limit is three hundred and ninety nine.
The number is eight thousand five hundred and sixty.

beats.on_screen: To find: the pattern in the last digit; the largest number below 399 in the count; is 8560 divisible by 5

marks.find: the three questions are written in a list

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find three things.
First, the pattern in the last digit.
<bookmark mark='second'/>Second, the largest number below the limit in the count.
Third, whether five divides the big number.

beats.on_screen: Step 1, last digits of 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30: 5, 0, 5, 0, 5, 0, so the last digit is 0 or 5

marks.digits: the last digit of each card is lit in turn
marks.turns: the digits 5 and 0 are shown taking turns

narration: <bookmark mark='digits'/>Step one, read the last digit of each number in the count.
<bookmark mark='turns'/>It goes five, zero, five, zero, five, zero.
The last digit is always zero or five.

beats.on_screen: Step 2, walk down from 399: 399 ends in 9, 398 in 8, 397 in 7, 396 in 6, 395 in 5

marks.down: the numbers 399 down to 395 appear one by one with their last digits lit
marks.more: 397 and 396 appear with their last digits lit
marks.stop: the first number ending in 0 or 5 is circled

narration: <bookmark mark='down'/>Step two, walk down from the limit, and read each last digit.
Three hundred and ninety nine ends in nine, three hundred and ninety eight in eight.
<bookmark mark='more'/>Three hundred and ninety seven ends in seven, and three hundred and ninety six in six.
<bookmark mark='stop'/>Three hundred and ninety five ends in five, so we stop there.

beats.on_screen: Step 3, 8560 ends in 0, so 5 divides it: 5 x 1712 = 8560

marks.last: the last digit 0 of 8560 lights up
marks.tick: 5 x 1712 = 8560 is written and a tick appears

narration: <bookmark mark='last'/>Step three, read the last digit of the big number. It is zero.
<bookmark mark='tick'/>Five divides it. Five times one thousand seven hundred and twelve is eight thousand five hundred and sixty.

beats.on_screen: Answer: the last digit is 0 or 5; 395; yes
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The last digit is zero or five.
The largest number is three hundred and ninety five.
And yes, five divides eight thousand five hundred and sixty.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the boxed answer
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's doubt in a bubble; the cards 10, 20 and 30 on the strip light up and the bubble is struck through

marks.doubt: the bubble appears over the strip
marks.zero: the cards 10, 20 and 30 light up with their zeros

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks only numbers ending in five are divisible by five.
<bookmark mark='zero'/>But ten, twenty and thirty are in the count of five, and they end in zero.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Both endings belong to the count, zero and five.
